rows.metric: Section 1031: gain not recognised on a like-kind exchange of real property
rows.value: Gain is not recognised; cash or other property received (“boot”) is taxed
rows.quote: Generally, if you make a like-kind exchange, you are not required to recognize a gain or loss under Internal Revenue Code Section 1031. If, as part of the exchange, you also receive other (not like-kind) property or money, you must recognize a gain to the extent of the other property and money received.
rows.note: Deferral, not forgiveness: the gain carries into the replacement property.

rows.metric: Section 1031 applies only to real property
rows.quote: Under the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, Section 1031 now applies only to exchanges of real property and not to exchanges of personal or intangible property.

rows.value: Any U.S. real property held for business or investment, improved or unimproved; not foreign property
rows.quote: Real properties generally are of like-kind, regardless of whether they’re improved or unimproved. … However, real property in the United States is not like-kind to real property outside the United States.
rows.note: A restaurant parcel can be exchanged into apartments, industrial, land or a diversified net-lease portfolio.

rows.quote: Proposition 13 requires assessment of each taxable property based on its fair market value and limits a property owner’s general levy tax to 1 percent of the assessed value.

rows.metric: Proposition 13 cap on annual growth in assessed value
rows.value: 2% a year, except on change in ownership or new construction
rows.quote: Proposition 13 mandated that a property’s assessed value could not increase by more than 2 percent from one year to the next except in the event of a change in ownership, new construction, the property receives a temporary decline in assessed value (Proposition 8), or the property is designated a restricted historical property (Mills Act).
rows.note: A sale resets the assessed value to the price paid. Under an NNN lease the TENANT pays that higher tax — so a long-held property with a low assessed value is cheaper for the tenant to occupy under the current owner than under a buyer.

rows.quote: In addition to the 1 percent general levy tax, the constitution allows for voter-approved indebtedness taxes and direct assessment taxes to pay for services such as schools, water districts, lighting maintenance, weed abatement, emergency services, etc.

rows.value: +23.6% in four years (5.4% a year); +6.5% in the latest year
rows.note: Arithmetic on INC-11. Nominal income per person has been rising faster than the 3.7% inflation rate — while the number of people falls.

rows.note: Added to the City tax.

rows.metric: City of Los Angeles transfer tax as published by the County Recorder
rows.value: $2.25 per $500, plus 4% of the total value above $5,400,000 and below $10,900,000, or 5.5% at or above $10,900,000
rows.quote: | Los Angeles (Effective 7/1/26) | 44 | $2.25 for each $500 or fraction thereof; AND EITHER 4 Percent of the total transaction value of sales above $5,400,000 but less than $10,900,000; OR 5.5 Percent of the total transaction value of sales at or above $10,900,000. |
rows.note: A second official source agreeing with the City's own page (TAX-02 to TAX-05), and confirming the tax is on the TOTAL value, not the excess.

rows.quote: | Los Angeles (Effective 7/1/25) | 44 | $2.25 for each $500 or fraction thereof; AND EITHER 4 Percent of the total transaction value of sales above $5,300,000 but less than $10,600,000; OR 5.5 Percent of the total transaction value of sales at or above $10,600,000. |
rows.note: The threshold rose $100,000 (1.9%) in the latest annual adjustment.

rows.metric: All transfer taxes on a City of Los Angeles sale
rows.value: 0.56% at or below $5.4 million; 4.56% above $5.4 million and below $10.9 million; 6.06% at or above $10.9 million
rows.note: Arithmetic on TAX-04/05/06 and TAX-10. At $5,400,001 the tax is about $246,000; at $5,400,000 it is about $30,000. A price in the band from $5.4 million to roughly $5.63 million nets the seller LESS than a price of exactly $5.4 million (5,400,000 × (1 − 0.0056) ÷ (1 − 0.0456) = $5,626,000, computed).
